title: AI / Agentic Systems Engineer
description:
**About UnderAI**

UnderAI is building AI\-powered software for the insurance industry. Our platform works with large and complex insurance documents and helps brokers automate workflows such as policy audits, RFQ creation, risk analysis, document comparison, and policy placement.

We are looking for an engineer who has hands\-on experience building \*agentic AI systems in production\*, not just calling an LLM API.

**What You’ll Work On**

You’ll work on production AI systems that reason over large documents, call tools, retrieve structured and unstructured information, and execute multi\-step workflows reliably.

You will work on problems such as:

\- Building and improving agentic workflows for insurance document processing.

\- Designing agents that can use tools safely and reliably.

\- Working with large\-context documents such as insurance policies, placement slips, RFQs, and exposure documents.

\- Building document extraction, retrieval, grounding, and comparison pipelines.

\- Implementing human\-in\-the\-loop workflows where users can review and approve AI decisions.

\- Designing evals to measure agent accuracy, tool usage, regressions, hallucinations, and reliability.

\- Improving prompt architecture, context management, and failure recovery.

\- Building structured outputs and validation layers around LLM responses.

\- Reducing hallucinations through grounding, deterministic checks, and verification systems.

\- Working closely with product and engineering teams to move AI features from prototype to production.

**What We’re Looking For**

You should have experience with several of the following:

\- Building LLM\-powered or agentic systems in production.

\- Tool calling / function calling.

\- Agent orchestration and multi\-step workflows.

\- RAG, embeddings, vector search, or hybrid retrieval.

\- Working with large documents or long\-context LLMs.

\- Structured output generation and schema validation.

\- Prompt engineering and context engineering.

\- LLM evaluation frameworks and regression testing.

\- Guardrails and prompt\-injection mitigation.

\- Human\-in\-the\-loop AI systems.

\- Experience working with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or similar model APIs.

**Engineering Skills**

Strong experience with:

\- TypeScript / Node.js or Python.

\- REST APIs and backend development.

\- PostgreSQL or similar relational databases.

\- Git and modern software engineering workflows.

Experience with the following is a plus:

\- Next.js

\- Drizzle / Prisma

\- LangGraph / LangChain or similar orchestration frameworks

\- Vector databases

\- PDF/document parsing

\- OCR and document intelligence

\- Background job systems and queues

\- Docker

\- Cloud deployments

**What Makes You Stand Out**

You’ve built an AI system where:

\- The model had access to tools.

\- Reliability mattered more than just producing a good demo.

\- You had to handle hallucinations and failures.

\- You built evals to measure performance.

\- You thought about prompt injection or tool security.

\- You had to reason over large amounts of context.

We care significantly more about \*what you have built\* than certifications or buzzwords.

Please include GitHub repositories, demos, or projects showing agentic systems you have worked on.

title: Cloud and DevSecOps Engineer
description:
**The Role: Cloud \& DevSecOps Engineer**

Day to day, that means designing and running our infrastructure across Google Cloud Platform and AWS, owning our GitLab CI/CD pipelines, and implementing the security controls that protect PHI and financial data.

This role has a deliberate growth path. You will start as the hands\-on engineer who builds and secures the platform. Over your first year, you will work alongside the team lead and an external compliance specialist. During that time you will take on increasing ownership of our HIPAA program and SOC 2 Type II attestation, moving from implementing controls to designing and leading them. The goal is that you become our security and compliance lead. We will fund necessary training to get you there.

If you want your infrastructure and security decisions to actually matter, and you want a path from senior engineer to program owner, this is that role.

**What You'll Do**

***Cloud Architecture: GCP and AWS***

* Design, deploy, and operate our SaaS infrastructure across GCP and AWS using HIPAA\-aligned reference architectures.
* Make sure every workload touching PHI runs only on HIPAA\-eligible services. Business Associate Agreements must be signed for each cloud account and project before any PHI lands.
* Implement network segmentation and VPC design, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS key management, and least\-privilege IAM across both clouds.
* Build everything as infrastructure\-as\-code with Terraform. Environments should be reproducible, reviewable, and auditable.

***DevOps and GitLab CI/CD***

* Own and improve our GitLab CI/CD pipelines end to end: build, test, scan, deploy.
* Integrate security scanning into the pipeline (SAST, dependency and SCA scanning, container and IaC scanning) without turning delivery into a crawl.
* Manage secrets, artifacts, and release processes securely. Keep PHI out of logs, caches, and lower environments.
* Support the development team. Good pipelines make other engineers faster, not slower.

***Security Engineering***

* Implement and maintain technical safeguards: phishing\-resistant MFA, centralized audit logging, monitoring and alerting, vulnerability management, and incident response.
* Enforce bastion or VDI\-only production access with no local download of PHI, backed by DLP and egress controls.
* Keep production access minimal and regularly reviewed. Use de\-identified or synthetic data in development and test environments.
* Respond to security events and lead post\-incident reviews.

***Compliance: HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II, Plaid***

*Starting out, you implement and evidence. Over time, you design and lead.*

* Implement the technical controls behind our HIPAA Security Rule safeguards and SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, then take ownership of the program as you grow into the role.
* Operate our compliance automation platform (Vanta, Drata, or Secureframe): keep evidence collection running, monitor for control drift, close gaps.
* Own the security side of our Plaid integration. That means TLS 1\.2\+ and mTLS where required, encrypted secrets, least\-privilege access to financial data, and monitoring for unauthorized access. You will also support Plaid's production access review and security questionnaire. Handling consumer financial data carries GLBA and FTC Safeguards Rule obligations, and you will help us meet them.
* Support penetration tests and audits: help scope them, coordinate with the testers and auditor, and drive remediation.
* Over time, you will lead the HIPAA risk analysis, own control design, select and manage the external auditor, and carry us through the SOC 2 Type II observation period.

**What You Need**

* 3\+ years in cloud engineering, DevOps, or DevSecOps.
* Hands\-on production experience on both GCP and AWS. Not one cloud plus a certification in the other: real production work in both.
* Strong GitLab CI/CD experience, or equivalent CI/CD depth and the ability to move to GitLab quickly.
* Terraform and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes).
* Practical security engineering: IAM and least privilege, encryption, secrets management, network security, logging and monitoring.
* Working exposure to HIPAA or SOC 2 in practice. You should be able to explain what a control is and how you'd evidence it.
* The judgment to handle PHI responsibly and work inside strict access controls.
* Clear written and spoken English. You will document data flows, controls, and decisions that auditors and customers read.

**Nice to Have**

* Prior work at a healthcare, fintech, or other regulated SaaS company handling sensitive data.
* Hands\-on experience with a compliance automation platform (Vanta, Drata, Secureframe, Sprinto).
* Experience integrating a financial data provider such as Plaid, and awareness of GLBA / FTC Safeguards Rule obligations.
* Any of these certifications: AWS Solutions Architect Professional, AWS Security Specialty, Google Professional Cloud Architect, Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer, CISSP, CCSP, CISM, HITRUST CCSFP.
* Experience working directly with external auditors or remediating penetration test findings.

title: Sales Engineer — Race Track Compliance Systems
description:
What we are building


**We are hiring a field team, in the hundreds.**
------------------------------------------------


Rural agriculture is short of people, and we have said so on our company page. It would be a hollow thing to argue that and then run this company from an office. Over the coming years we intend to hire hundreds into the field — people who work in the districts where the animals are, alongside the farmers and dairy staff who care for them.


*01***Field\-deployed data scientists**
Not data scientists who visit a farm. Data scientists based near the herds, who calibrate models against the animals in front of them, and who will know within a week when a model is wrong because they will be standing next to the reason.


*02***Agriculture interns**
Agriculture and veterinary graduates who want their first year of work to be spent in sheds and yards rather than in a training room. We would rather teach data science to someone who understands cattle than the reverse.


*03***Field technicians**
Fitting, servicing and commissioning sensors and gateways, and training the caretakers who use them. Hired in the district, trained by us, working with the same farms year after year.


What we screen for, before any qualification


* You like the people who do this work. Farmers, dairy staff, goshala caretakers, stockmen — not as beneficiaries of your expertise, but as the ones who know things you do not.
* You will go to the animal. The best model in this company was improved by somebody who noticed something in a shed, not in a notebook.
* You can explain it so a farmer understands it. If a recommendation does not land in plain words, in her language, it has not landed.
* You will say when the data is wrong. We would rather hear it from you than from a veterinarian, and far rather than from a trustee.
Hiring at this scale happens district by district and follows deployments, not the other way round. We do not open a role in a place we are not working, and we do not fly people in to a district where somebody local could do the job better.


If you are reading this and none of the roles listed below is yours, write anyway. Tell us the district you know and what you have done in it.


  
How to apply


Send your resume and a short cover letter to **hr@hanuinnotech.com** or **svuppalapati@hanuinnotech.com**, with the role title in the subject line.
  
Before the résumé


We hire people who are willing to stand in a shed in the rain and then go home and improve a model.*Both halves matter. A model built by someone who has never stood in the rain gets the wrong things right. A day in the rain that does not change the model helps one farm once.*


**What we ask of everyone**
---------------------------


Sales Engineers, Field Engineers, Data Interns and Business Development Account Executives — whatever the title, the same things are non\-negotiable.


01
#### **Love to see farmers succeed**


Not tolerate it. Not serve it as a market. Actually want it, and be visibly pleased when a herd comes through a bad season because somebody acted on an alert. If a farmer's win does not feel like your win, this is the wrong company.


02
#### **Understand the farmer and their pain points**


Sit with them. Learn what the season costs, what the loan repayment falls due against, why the last technology they were sold is in a drawer. You cannot solve a problem you have only read about, and nobody here gets to design for a farm they have never stood on.


03
#### **Explain it so a farmer understands it**


Every recommendation must land in plain words, in their own language, in the time they have between milkings. If it needs a slide deck to make sense, it is not finished. Clarity is not a courtesy here — it is the product working.


04
#### **Own the problem to the outcome**


Passion to own the problem end to end, and to make sure the customer actually succeeds — with benefits you can point at, for farmers, banks, insurance providers and every customer we serve. Not a handover. Not a ticket closed. The result.


05
#### **Feel what a four\-legged customer cannot say**


We need people who feel the pain of our four\-legged customers, and who serve the humans who dearly love them. Animals must be treated humanely, and you play an important role in that — a role we reward.


06
#### **Persistent, and willing to think outside the box**


Rural deployment does not go to plan. Networks fail, seasons turn, the obvious answer is often the wrong one. We need people who stay with a problem after it becomes inconvenient, and who look for the answer nobody in the room has suggested yet.


How this shows up in what you are paid


If farmers' revenue increases, you are paid a bonus. If animals are treated humanely and you played a part in it, you are rewarded. We tie reward to the outcomes we say we care about, because a mission that costs nothing to ignore is not a mission.


You are working for more than a pay


Every person here is working towards something larger than the salary: real difference in the world, and a future in which the next generation has opportunity where they already live.


A young person in Anand or Srinagar or Vizianagaram should not have to leave for a city to find work worth doing. If the analytics that make a herd profitable are built where the herd is, the work stays there too. Localised opportunity is not a by\-product of this business — it is the point of it.


And what is built locally travels. The models trained on a Kashmir winter serve temperate Europe and Central Asia. The mango forecasts built for Philippine smallholders serve a global bottler. Local opportunity and global prosperity are the same project, run in the right order.


We hire for this before we hire for the résumé. The technical skill can be taught; this cannot.


  
Equine roles


### **For the horse sensor roles specifically**


Sales Engineers and Account Executives promoting the Hayagriva HG Model 3 must be able to hold a credible conversation with four very different rooms, often in the same week.


**Race club owners**
Commercial owners of racing clubs and yards, who will ask what the sensor protects and what it costs against the value of the animal.


**Government agencies**
Procurement, welfare and compliance officers buying at institutional scale, with the process and documentation that requires.


**Police and military units**
Mounted police and military or ceremonial establishments, where the animal is operational and readiness is the requirement.


**Professional race trainers**
The people closest to the horse, who will judge the product on whether it tells them something they did not already know.


The finding these roles rest on


Tracks that publish their injury data record roughly a third fewer fatalities than tracks that do not — 0\.88 against 1\.27 per 1,000 starts. The act of measuring, in public, is associated with the animals coming home. That is the whole argument for a sensor on a horse: not that any single injury was preventable, but that a yard which watches continuously sees more than a yard which watches at exercise.


If you cannot say that sentence to a steward and mean every word of it, these are not your roles.


  
The person who makes it work on the ground. You install HG sensors across a club's stabled population, prove the data holds through a racing season, and turn it into a compliance record the club's stewards will accept.


Responsibilities


* Design and deliver HG Sensor deployments across a club's yards, from pilot to full population
* Install, commission and service sensors, and run the calibration that teaches the models each animal
* Build the injury and welfare reporting a club needs for its stewards, its regulator and — where it chooses — publication
* Specify HG Sensor Core or HG Sensor Enterprise on\-site hosting where a club cannot or will not connect to an outside network
* Train club staff, trainers, grooms and veterinary teams on what the alerts mean and what to do about them
* Sit at the track on race days and see whether the system earned its place
What we look for


* Engineering or data science background, with hands\-on comfort — you will be fitting hardware, not presenting slides about it
* Able to explain a model's output to a trainer in the words a trainer uses
* Comfortable around horses and trained, or willing to be trained, in safe handling
* Willing to travel across Indian race centres and work to a racing calendar rather than an office one
* Understands that a claim you cannot support costs more than a sale you did not make

Every delayed email, broken link, or missed follow\-up can erode trust \- and in placements, trust is everything. That’s why we’re constantly refining the way we operate, and hence, you’d be:  

* Utilizing an array of tools, softwares, and platforms to automate processes in order to minimize human intervention and ensuring a flawless and effortless delivery of our placement cycles.
* Facilitating seamless collaboration with the product team to introduce innovative platform features and enhance operational efficiency.

 **Monthly Outcomes:**  

* **Month 1:** Understand all current placement processes, tools, and workflows. Assist in 2\-3 drives and begin managing recruiter and student interactions.
* **Month 2:** Run 3\-4 recruiter accounts independently with 90%\+ student participation and \<24hr query response time. Identify 3\-5 process gaps.
* **Month 3\+:** Implement at least 2 process improvements. Maintain Recruiter and Student NPS. Drive at least one automation initiative.

***A question we’d like to address upfront is what the career trajectory looks like for someone in this role.***  

At Kraftshala, operations are central to how we serve our stakeholders. You'll start by learning the craft of partnerships and account management through hands\-on placement execution. Over time, two broad paths could open up:  

* If your strengths lie in scaling processes, systems thinking, and managing cross\-functional execution, you could lead placement operations \- shaping how we deliver outcomes to recruiters and students at scale.
* If you love building and growing relationships, you could transition into owning large recruiter portfolios and driving new partnerships, repeat engagement, and even leading B2B initiatives.


These are starting thoughts, of course, and any decision on a role is always a function of what a person wants matched with what the organization can offer at that time. The great advantage of a company that’s growing well (like Kraftshala) is that new opportunities open up frequently, and our preference would always be to try to fill up newly created roles with candidates from within the organization. **Must\-Haves:**  

* 0\-2 years of prior experience in process management, relationship building, operations, or similar customer\-facing roles (We’re not fussed about the exact years of experience, as that’s just a proxy for your skill level.)
* Prior experience managing career services, placements, or corporate relations in an education institution would be a big plus

 **Top Grading:**  

We’re looking for someone who doesn't wait around for instructions to get started. Our A\-Players are those who take initiative \- they build relationships with all stakeholders, spot gaps early, and design solutions proactively. They are the ones who take full ownership of the student and recruiter experience, staying a few steps ahead of any possible issues.  

A B\-Player, on the other hand, might wait for work to be assigned or limit themselves to what's been explicitly stated. They may execute tasks well, but aren't thinking beyond what's in front of them \- which doesn't quite cut it in a high\-ownership, high\-trust team like ours. **Recruitment Process:**  

As a small team, we must get to know each other before taking the leap. We want to ensure you succeed in your role within our team. Each conversation with us will last about 30\-60 minutes, and will be a mix of online and in\-person interactions.  

* **Conversation 1:** This will be a virtual call with the HR team to understand your profile briefly and share the details of the selection process to set expectations about what you’re signing up for
* **Technical Exercise:** This is a specific assessment designed to evaluate your fit for this role
* **Conversation 2:** This will be a detailed assessment review conversation with the Operations team to go over your submission for the technical exercise.
* **Conversation 3:** This will be a conversation where you can expect to be further evaluated on the competencies needed for the job (mentioned above).
* **Conversation 4:** A conversation with our CEO to ensure that there is a fit with the Kraftshala Kode (read below about it).
* **Extending an offer:** If all goes well, we will extend an offer that will mention the relevant details.
